what_its_for: Pegcetacoplan is used to treat certain blood and eye conditions. Empaveli treats a rare blood disorder called paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), where your immune system destroys your red blood cells. Syfovre treats geographic atrophy (GA), a serious eye condition that causes vision loss related to age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Both conditions involve a part of your immune system called the complement system becoming overactive and causing damage.
how_to_take: Empaveli (for PNH): This medicine is given as a slow injection under your skin (subcutaneous infusion) using a small pump. You or a caregiver will be trained to do this at home. Each infusion takes about 30 minutes and is given in your belly area. Always rotate injection sites and never inject into skin that is sore, bruised, red, or scarred. Syfovre (for GA): This medicine is given as an injection directly into your eye by your eye doctor in a clinic. You should not try to give this injection yourself.
dosing: Empaveli (PNH): The usual dose is 1,080 mg injected under the skin twice a week. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well it works for you. Syfovre (GA): The usual dose is 15 mg injected into the affected eye once a month or once every other month, as directed by your eye doctor. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions for your dose and schedule.
missed_dose: Empaveli (PNH): If you miss a dose, give it as soon as you remember, then continue with your regular schedule. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue as normal. Do not give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor if you are unsure what to do. Syfovre (GA): If you miss your scheduled eye injection appointment, contact your eye doctor right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not try to self-inject.
storage: Empaveli (PNH): Store the vials in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep them in the original box to protect from light. Do not freeze. If needed, you may keep the vials at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 6 months, but do not put them back in the refrigerator after that. Keep all medicines out of reach of children. Syfovre (GA): This medicine is stored and handled by your eye doctor's office or clinic. You do not need to store it at home.
what_to_avoid: Avoid skipping your vaccinations. Because this medicine affects your immune system, you are at higher risk for serious infections, especially meningococcal infections (a dangerous type of bacterial infection). Make sure you are vaccinated against meningococcal bacteria, Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcal), and Haemophilus influenzae type B before starting treatment. Avoid contact with people who have serious infections. Tell your doctor right away if you develop signs of infection such as fever, chills, headache, stiff neck, or sensitivity to light. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause serious problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room immediately if you experience: fever, headache, stiff neck, nausea, vomiting, or sensitivity to light (signs of meningitis or serious infection); sudden change in vision, eye pain, redness, or increased sensitivity to light (signs of eye infection or other serious eye problems after injection); dark or cola-colored urine, sudden back pain, or extreme tiredness (signs that PNH may be getting worse); chest pain or shortness of breath; any new or unusual symptoms. Also call your doctor if you have questions about how to give your infusion or if you notice anything unusual at the injection site.
when_it_works: Empaveli (PNH): Many patients start to see improvement in their symptoms, such as less fatigue and fewer episodes of dark urine, within a few weeks. However, it may take several weeks to see the full benefit. Do not stop taking it even if you feel better. Syfovre (GA): This medicine works to slow down the progression of vision loss over time. You may not notice a big difference right away since it works gradually. It does not restore vision that has already been lost, but it can help protect the vision you still have. Regular follow-up visits with your eye doctor are very important.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: The safety and effectiveness of Empaveli in children under 18 years old has not been fully established. Syfovre is intended for adults only. Older adults: No special dose adjustment is typically needed for older adults, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver problems, as this may affect how your doctor monitors your treatment.
